extracted.intended_audience: general readers and reformers interested in social criticism, prison reform, and philanthropic policy
extracted.subtask_description: A close-reading of a Victorian-era social-criticism essay discussing prisons, philanthropy, and reform priorities; useful for readers or analysts extracting policy and moral claims about charitable practice and penal systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice over sentimentality
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice, Justice: woe betides us everywhere when, for this reason or for that, we fail to do justice! ... There is but one thing needed for the world; but that one is indispensable. Justice, Justice, in the name of Heaven; give us Justice, and we live; give us only counterfeits of it, or succedanea for it, and we die!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author argues that benevolence without justice is harmful: philanthropic gestures that substitute for justice will spread harm like a poison-tree. Reform efforts should ensure justice as the foundational criterion rather than mere sentimental aid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target aid to the 'not yet' enlisted (teachables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Yonder, in those dingy habitations, and shops of red herring and tobacco-pipes, where men have not yet quite declared for the Devil; there, I say, is land: here is mere sea-beach. Thither go with your benevolence, thither to those dingy caverns of the poor; and there instruct and drill and manage, there where some fruit may come from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate philanthropic resources where there's a realistic prospect of improvement — the poor who have not irrevocably fallen into vice — rather than the incorrigible. Focus on populations with potential to benefit from instruction and support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid wasting resources on incorrigible 'scoundrels' (the Devil's regiments)
rubrics_metrics.description: These are of the worst substance for enduring pressure! ... These select Few, as I explain to you, are they who have fallen to Chaos, and are sworn into certain regiments of the line ... A superior proclivity to Chaos is declared in these, by the very fact of their being here!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay warns against investing in individuals described as 'unteachables' or long-enlisted criminals: such investments often yield zero or negative returns, and may actively damage deserving recipients by drawing away scarce resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer practical, workmanlike reformers (the John Howard model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Howard is a beautiful Philanthropist ... John Howard, without pay in money, did this of the Jail-fever ... A man full of English accuracy; English veracity, solidity, simplicity; by whom this universal Jail-commission ... is set about, with all the slow energy, the patience, practicality, sedulity and sagacity common to the best English commissioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value measured, empirical, and persistent methods over sentimental or showy philanthropy. Practical inspection, record-keeping, and laborious attention to detail (e.g., weighing rations) are praised as effective reform practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure outcomes concretely
rubrics_metrics.description: When your jailer answers, 'The prisoner's allowance of food is so and so; and we observe it sacredly; here, for example, is a ration.'--'Hey! A ration this?' and solid John suddenly produces his weighing-scales; weighs it, marks down in his tablets what the actual quantity of it is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reform efforts should include concrete measurement and verification of promised services and resources. Empirical checks (weighing rations, documenting conditions) are necessary to ensure effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not replace substantive reform with 'benevolent-platform' sentimentality
rubrics_metrics.description: Howard abated the Jail-fever; but it seems to me he has been the innocent cause of a far more distressing fever ... the Benevolent-Platform Fever ... abolition of punishment, all-absorbing 'prison-discipline,' and general morbid sympathy, instead of hearty hatred, for scoundrels ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware of movements that prioritize emotional or rhetorical displays of philanthropy (platform speeches, subscriptions) over substantive, often unglamorous reforms. Sentiment can substitute for action and undermine social order if not grounded in practical justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize systemic public-health and sanitation measures
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Whitewash your scoundrel-population; sweep out your abominable gutters ... do these two things;--and observe, much cheaper if you please!' ... There is perhaps some endeavor to do a little scavengering; and, as the all-including point, to cheapen the terrible cost of Government
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic civic measures like street-cleaning, scavenging, and public sanitation are presented as essential, cost-effective reforms that should take precedence over futile attempts to rehabilitate hardened criminals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold reform leaders and 'quacks' accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: And, above all and inclusive of all, cannot you go to those Solemn human Shams, Phantasm Captains, and Supreme Quacks that ride prosperously in every thoroughfare; and with severe benevolence, ask them, What they are doing here?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and confront self-styled reformers and influential figures whose actions produce the 'waters of bitterness.' Stopping harmful leadership or culture (the fountain) can be more effective than diffuse charity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect merit and avoid unjust patronage
rubrics_metrics.description: On the whole, what a reflection is it that we cannot bestow on an unworthy man any particle of our benevolence ... without withdrawing it ... from one worthy, to whom it of right belongs! ... I give the cobbling of my boots to incompetent Duncan M'Pastehorn ... withdraws the job from sober, plainly competent, and meritorious Mr. Sparrowbill ... clearly tending to the ruin of poor Sparrowbill!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charitable or patronage decisions should not undermine deserving, competent individuals by rewarding incompetence. Justice in allocation of opportunities preserves social incentives and prevents wider harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence educational effort: teach the teachable first
rubrics_metrics.description: If I had schoolmasters, my benevolent friend, do you imagine I would set them on teaching a set of unteachables ... Minds open to that particular conviction are not the material I like to work upon. When once my schoolmasters have gone over all the other classes of society from top to bottom ... I will then send them to operate on these regiments of the line: then, and, assure yourself, never till then.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate educational resources in phases, prioritizing populations most likely to benefit; delay dedicating scarce teaching resources to those judged deeply incorrigible until other groups have been served.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate discipline for incorrigibles when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: By 'love,' without hope except of peaceably teasing oakum, or fear except of a temporary loss of dinner, he was to guide these men ... A collar round the neck, and a cart-whip flourished over the back; these, in a just and steady human hand, were what the gods would have appointed them; and now when, by long misconduct and neglect, they had sworn themselves into the Devil's regiments ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay endorses employing firm disciplinary measures (hard drill, punitive systems) for those assessed as beyond reform, arguing that lenient methods alone will not reclaim such individuals and may leave society worse off.
